newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 7.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Four people died and scores were injured in clashes between police and residents protesting against rates and service charges in coloured townships and around Johannesburg yesterday.
- Telkom is to face competition in April 2002, by which time it must roll out at least 1.8-milliom lines and turn around its much-criticised customer service record or face hefty penalties.
- Senior government representatives moved yesterday to put a damper on expectations about a dramatic announcement on exchange controls when Presiodent Nelson Mandela opens palrliament.

- Armscor has announced a new affirmative procurement policy which will see previously disadvantaged companies paid up to 12 percent more than white companies when awarded defence equipment contracts.

- Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma voiced support for research on AIDS drug Virodence yesterday despite the fact that it contained a toxic industrial solvent, prompting suggestions that a "paraffina" debacle was imminent.
BUSINESS REPORT

- North West Development Corporation defended its chairman, Khehla Mthembu, yesterday from allegations that he had betrayed black business by accepting an appointment as non-executive chairman of Sun International South Africa, in which North West has a significant shreholdings.

- The rand strengthened and the JSE traded the highest value of shares in its 109-year history yesterday on strong expectations that President Nelson Mandela's fourth opening address to parliament today would spur South Africa's economy, dealers said.
- Ernst & Young, the auditing firm, has committed itself to a 25 percent black shareholding within the next three years, Tom Wixley, the chairman of Ernst & Young, said yesterday.
- Nickel prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) have moved up rapidly this year after a period of sustained low values, signalling a recovery in the stainless steel market, analysts said.
SAKE BEELD
- Telkom faces competition over the next five years. It must have greater client services.
- Malbak is unbundling and will become a British and South African packaging group.
THE STAR

- At least three people were killed and hundreds injured yesterday when security forces clashed with residents from coloured communities in southern and western Johannesburg, protesting against what they claim to be excessive rent and service charges.
- Dr Wouter Basson, the chemical warfare expert arrested in a drug bust last week, has also been linked to medical experiments on humans.
